chapter: Bolden and the road to New Orleans
title: Make Me a Pallet on the Floor as a spiritual or Bolden song
summary: They debate whether the song began as a spiritual; Ory first heard it from Bolden.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: I heard that at Belmore, New Jersey.

60 years behind what happened, you know. I had to guess, you know, guest artists on the show. Same darn thing. Wasn't in the name for it. We invited things as one. We used to go over and listen. That's a nice, you know. That's been going on since I was a kid.
Well, was Make Me a Pallet on the floor?
A spiritual before it was a...
Well, the first one I played was Bowlin, and he claimed it, so... Well, that was Bowlin's song. It was.
That's a profane song, if I ever heard of it. I thought maybe...
Yeah, I don't think it would fit in the church. I thought maybe that's... Not in the lyrics, no way.
Unless they added a new lyric, you know.
After all, it was about an illicit love affair. I know, but I thought maybe, you know, Bowlin had added different lyrics to it or something like that.
No, he did everything. But a lot of the numbers that they whipped up, they took old classical folk songs and all sorts of things and changed them over.
